title: Ant on the Boundary
summary: An ant starts at a boundary and moves left or right based on the values in an array of non-zero integers.
statement: An ant starts at a boundary and moves left or right based on the values in an array of non-zero integers. It counts the number of times it returns to the boundary after moving according to the array values. The ant checks the boundary only after moving the absolute value of the current element, not during the movement.
constraints: An ant starts at boundary position zero.
Each value is its signed movement during one time step.
Count how many step endpoints place the ant back at position zero; the initial position does not count.
hints: Maintain the ant’s current coordinate as a running prefix sum.
Increment the answer whenever the new prefix sum equals zero.
The coordinate after each step is exactly its prefix sum, so zero prefixes correspond one-for-one with counted returns.
editorial: The coordinate after each step is exactly its prefix sum, so zero prefixes correspond one-for-one with counted returns.

tests.explanation: The prefix positions are two, five, and zero, so the boundary is reached once.
The prefix positions are three, five, two, and negative two, never zero.
